title: partner-cloud-marketplace-weekly-sync-prep-jamie-2026-03-16
content:
Weekly partner & cloud marketplace sync — prep notes (internal)
Date: 2026-03-16 10:00am PT
Attendees (expected): Jamie Nguyen (Redwood), Sara Li (AWS PM), Rohit Mehta (GCP Partner Eng), Luis Garcia (Azure BD), Priya Shah (Redwood BD), Marco Ruiz (Redwood Solutions)

Goals for this sync:
- Align on AWS marketplace listing timeline and missing artifacts
- Validate GCP Workload Identity flow & IAM mapping for private deployments
- Confirm Azure co-sell eligibility checklist progress
- Surface any technical or legal hold-ups that block marketplace launches
- Agree on immediate next steps + owners for partner kickoff (w/in 2 weeks)

Agenda (30–40 min)
1) Quick status round (5 min) — each partner: green/yellow/red, top 1 ask
2) AWS listing items (10 min)
   - Current status: draft listing uploaded 2026-03-10, awaiting security questionnaire and billing contact
   - Open items: security questionnaire (SOC2 scoping), finalized product screenshots, pricing matrix for Dedicated plans
   - Risk: billing contact + tax docs delay could push launch by 2+ weeks
3) GCP integration (8 min)
   - Workload Identity verification: partner needs service account mapping example (we provide), they need to test end-to-end with a sample private deployment
   - Billing/invoicing: discuss if partner wants consolidated billing or per-customer usage reports
4) Azure co-sell / marketplace (5 min)
   - Co-sell checklist: legal sign-off, Azure-certified container images, performance benchmarks required by Azure marketplace
5) Go-to-market & enablement (5 min)
   - Joint webinar timelines, PR assets, solution brief deadlines
6) Action items / next steps (2–5 min)

Key metrics / current numbers to call out
- Marketplace MRR (all partners combined): $62k/month (Feb 2026) — up 18% MoM
- Trial-to-paid conversion via marketplace listing: 7.8% (last 30 days)
- Average provisioning time (private deploy via partner flow): 4.5 days (goal: <48 hrs)
- Number of active listings: AWS=1 (staging), GCP=0, Azure=0

Detailed notes / talking points
- AWS: need to confirm the exact list of screenshots they accept (console + billing + config). Marco to create a screenshot checklist and capture 2 sample flows (hosted API + VPC private deployment). We should push for a single SKU with metered billing for hosted API plus a separate plan for Dedicated reserved capacity. Sara asked for pricing tiers — Jamie to propose 3-tier pricing (startup, scale, enterprise) and sample usage scenarios by Tue 2026-03-17.
- GCP: Rohit emphasized Workload Identity docs must include role bindings examples and a short troubleshooting doc for common IAM errors. Priya to prioritize a simple runbook (aim EOD 2026-03-18). Also need to decide whether to use GCP Marketplace's private offer flow or direct contract + listing; follow-up item for Rohit to share recommended path.
- Azure: Luis flagged container image security scans as a blocker — need SBOM and vulnerability scan report. Engineering (Marco) to run a quick scan and attach SBOM by 2026-03-19.
- Legal / tax: AWS requested tax / billing contact for reseller agreement. Jamie to coordinate with finance (Elaine Wu) and provide contact + docs by 2026-03-18.

Risks / blockers (to call out)
- Delay in security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence) — worst-case pushes AWS public listing by 3+ weeks.
- Lack of automation in provisioning (currently manual onboarding tickets) — impacts SLA promises for partner-driven installs.
- Incomplete performance benchmark report for Azure — need to run 1–2 high-concurrency tests and capture latency percentiles.

Asks for partners (what we need from them during or after meeting)
- AWS: confirm billing contact & tax info; review proposed pricing tiers; accept draft listing assets by 2026-03-20
- GCP: sign off on workload identity test plan and confirm preferred billing flow by 2026-03-19
- Azure: provide container scan acceptance criteria and co-sell form signer by 2026-03-20

Action items (flat list with owners & due dates)
- AI-1: Create AWS screenshot checklist + capture 2 demo flows (hosted + private) — owner: Marco Ruiz — due: 2026-03-18
- AI-2: Draft 3-tier pricing proposal + example usage scenarios — owner: Jamie Nguyen — due: 2026-03-17
- AI-3: Provide SOC2 evidence summary and answer AWS questionnaire (coordinate with Elaine Wu in finance) — owner: Jamie Nguyen / Elaine Wu — due: 2026-03-18
- AI-4: Produce GCP workload identity runbook (role binding examples + troubleshooting) — owner: Priya Shah — due: 2026-03-18
- AI-5: Run container security scan, generate SBOM & attach report for Azure review — owner: Marco Ruiz / Eng infra — due: 2026-03-19
- AI-6: Rohit to advise on GCP marketplace vs private-offer path and recommended next steps — owner: Rohit Mehta (GCP) — due: 2026-03-19
- AI-7: Draft joint webinar outline + required assets list — owner: Priya Shah — due: 2026-03-25
- AI-8: Triage automation for provisioning (quick wins list) — owner: Marco Ruiz / Solutions Eng — due: 2026-03-23

Follow-up plan
- After sync: update Confluence page MARKETPLACE-ONBOARDING-4321 with confirmed artifacts and attach screenshot checklist + SBOM
- Weekly check-in thread on Slack (#partner-marketplace) for progress updates on AI list; call out any slipped dates
- Schedule a 30-min technical deep dive with AWS technical account manager next week if SOC2 questions remain open (tentative: 2026-03-22)

Open questions / TBD
- Should we use marketplace metered billing for Dedicated reserved capacity or handle Dedicated via contracts & link from listing? (impacts revenue recognition + billing flows)
- Do partners require specific sample customers/use-cases per region for co-sell approval? Who will collect these case studies?

Notes to self (scratchpad)
- Keep the meeting tight: 30–40 min and focus on unblockers only
- Bring the 3-tier pricing slides and sample screenshots to reduce back-and-forth
- If AWS pushes for more SOC2 detail, escalate to Emily (Head of Security) and request a rapid evidence bundle

End of prep notes.
